games.note: The most-visited page on the site and the worst converting: 454 sessions produced 1 game_start and 7 Players. No Post of ours sent this traffic, so the arrivals are coming from somewhere we are not measuring.
Almost all of this is the paid Facebook Trial: 1,587 of the 1,630 impressions and 105 of the 105 clicks. Best play rate of any Game with real traffic.
No signal from the Post (16 impressions). GA4 reports 29 Players against 18 sessions, which is not a rate — see the tracking anomaly.

topAngles.angle: the battery is the health bar
topAngles.evidence: 1,587 impressions, 105 link clicks, 6.62% CTR at $0.005 per click in under a day. Every other angle this week is below 100 impressions and unreadable.

anomalies.evidence: The Facebook Campaign reports 105 inline_link_clicks; GA4 attributes 10 sessions and 3 Players to utm_content=fb-ad-1. Nine out of ten paid clicks never became a measured visit.

anomalies.what: road-rumble takes 454 sessions and produces 1 game_start
anomalies.evidence: 454 sessions, 1 game_start, 7 Players, playRate 1.5% — the largest traffic source on the site and the lowest conversion. No Post of ours sent it.

anomalies.what: Players exceed sessions on three pages
anomalies.evidence: carrom 29 Players / 18 sessions (161%), post plan-wednesday 22 Players / 11 sessions (200%), ennead 10 / 12 (83%). played_30s is counted as eventCount against session-scoped dimensions, so playRate above 100% is an artefact, not a result.

anomalies.what: game_start disagrees with played_30s in both directions
anomalies.evidence: drift: 0 game_starts but 31 Players. sync: 15 game_starts but 0 Players and 11 sessions. The event cannot be used as a funnel step until it agrees with the other two.

anomalies.what: Organic reach on X has collapsed
anomalies.evidence: 5 Posts, 124 impressions in total, 1 link click. The best single Post reached 58 people. Nothing organic cleared the 100-impression signal floor.

anomalies.what: The Facebook Post's impressions have never been read
anomalies.evidence: fb-metrics.json records the ennead Post with impressions null and an insights error; every Facebook reach number is currently unknown rather than zero.

recommendations.do: Treat the click-to-session gap on the Facebook Campaign as the first thing to fix, before spending more.
recommendations.because: 105 clicks produced 10 sessions and 3 Players. At $0.005 per click the Campaign looks like the cheapest traffic we have ever bought, but the measured cost per Player is $0.17 and 90% of what we paid for is unaccounted. Either the landing is dropping people or the utm is being stripped; until we know which, every paid decision rests on a number we cannot trust.

recommendations.do: Move the publishing Windows to 19:00-21:00 UTC.
recommendations.because: Players by hour peak at 21:00 UTC with 28, then 23:00 with 11, and 19:00 and 20:00 with 9 each. The three Windows we actually publish in — 09, 13 and 17 UTC — collected 1, 2 and 1 Players respectively. We are publishing into the four quietest hours of the day.

recommendations.do: Investigate road-rumble's landing page before promoting it.
recommendations.because: 454 sessions — more than every other Game combined — turned into 1 game_start and 7 Players. Whatever is sending that traffic, the page is not converting it, and paying to send more would be the most expensive mistake available.

recommendations.do: Give the paid slot to drift and let its Trial finish.
recommendations.because: drift is the only Game with both real traffic and a real play rate: 294 sessions, 31 Players, 10.5%. Its Campaign is running at 6.62% CTR, 26 times the 0.25% kill threshold, on $0.52 spent so far.

recommendations.do: Stop counting playRate as a percentage until played_30s and sessions are reconciled.
recommendations.because: Three pages report over 100%, one at 200%. Any ranking built on this number today can invert once it is fixed.

recommendations.do: Do not read anything into this week's organic Posts.
recommendations.because: Every one of the five X Posts is under the 100-impression floor (58, 33, 16, 10, 7). There is no signal to act on, and treating the carrom Post's 6.25% CTR as a result would be reading one click.

paidReadiness.angle: the battery is the health bar
paidReadiness.why: The only Game that both attracts traffic and retains it: 294 sessions, 31 Players, 10.5% play rate, and a live Campaign converting at 6.62% CTR for half a cent a click. carrom's play rate is nominally higher but rests on 18 sessions and a broken ratio; road-rumble has the traffic and does not convert it.
